impact: All 4 rows are status='pending' and are the newest in their tables, so they render at the TOP of the admin Access-requests and Nominee-claims queues, and they inflate the admin 'Needs attention' pending-access-requests count from 4 to 6. A rep opening either queue today sees 'A24XSSPROBE ' as the first row. Separately, if any of those admin surfaces renders the field unescaped (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html-equivalent, or an unescaped CSV/PDF export), this is a live stored XSS — A24 owns the render-side confirmation; this finding establishes that the payloads ARE stored and ARE reachable. No pre-existing junk exists anywhere in the schema: these 4 rows are the entire hit set.
suggested_fix: Delete the 4 probe rows before any demo: DELETE FROM public.access_requests WHERE id IN ('ar-1787558699527-rmm4','ar-1787558701196-dksm'); DELETE FROM public.nominee_claims WHERE id IN ('nc-bbf6090b4d1d48e991f65357be9e62f1','nc-d810114b14304a0f85c0337cdfa21ac3'); — after A24 has finished its render-side verification. Longer term, add server-side length + character validation on the public request-access and nominee-claim forms (both are unauthenticated write paths with no bound on content).
